What the KB encoding provably carries — and what the GNN adds

Linear probes read ground-truth world-state out of z, scored on held-out episodes; z (full comms) vs z with the comm graph cut.

setattn + role checkpoints · probes fit on training maps, scored on unseen maps · the map below is one held-out episode · z=full comms, z₀=comms cut (GNN contributes nothing).

How to read this
Ledger (right): each property's bar is the held-out R² of a linear probe decoding that true quantity from the encoding — z = full comms, z₀ = comms cut. The red tick is the shuffled-label chance level. A tall z with a much shorter z₀ (marked GNN) means that fact reaches the agent only through communication — the GNN verified. Trace (below map): the value the probe reads out of z vs. the truth, over the held-out episode; where they diverge is the anomaly signal.
t=0
held-out episode (fog = this agent's KB) — green=known · slate=wall · amber=sensed now · ring=comm · dashed=comm link · ●=selected agent
solid=true · dashed=read from z · faint=read from z₀ (comms cut). Gap between solid and dashed = probe error / anomaly signal.
